title: REPORT on the implementation of the EU agri-food promotion policy
part_text: 5. Stresses the need to continue to earmark resources to accompany the marketing of exported products covered by promotion programmes, with a particular focus on third countries, as this would ensure the greater visibility and competitiveness of the agricultural sector; underlines the importance of highlighting Europe’s high production standards and the distinctive qualities of European agricultural and food products, including food safety, traceability, environmental requirements, animal welfare standards, authenticity, labelling, nutritional aspects, and quality requirements, thereby strengthening consumer confidence and enhancing the competitiveness of EU products, particularly with regard to their quality, diversity, and traditions; stresses that this is of particular relevance in the light of recent trade agreements and the need to promote a level playing field with imported products; highlights the potential of funding to support small and medium-sized producers in participating in agri-food fairs, thereby strengthening their market reach and visibility;
